file: app/globals.css (the theme blocks), and the tile
what: Dark is the default. Two theme blocks and no system copy: bare :root holds the dark values with color-scheme: dark, and :root[data-theme="light"] holds the light ones with color-scheme: light. There is no @media (prefers-color-scheme) block, so with no data-theme the page is dark under a light system too. (Brief 103 already asks for these two blocks in globals.css.)

file: lib/theme-preference.ts and components/shell/ThemeMenu.tsx (both new in brief 103, tasks 9 and 10)
what: BEHAVIOUR, for the product manager. No stored choice means Dark, not Auto: resolveTheme returns dark when nothing is stored, the boot script stamps dark, and the account menu shows Dark checked on a first visit. Auto stays as a third choice; picking it stores the word auto, and only then does the app follow the system. Brief 103 says the opposite today ("absent means Auto"), which opens light on a light system.
The tile's control reads Dark, Light, Auto. Dark is pressed on load and the line under it says "Showing the dark theme."
The tile's script: Light sets data-theme="light", Dark removes data-theme, Auto sets or removes it to follow the system. A data-theme the hosting page sets is followed.

A link keeps color: var(--color-accent), which is the ink now, and gets a thin grey underline: text-decoration-color: var(--color-neutral-600), text-decoration-thickness: var(--size-underline). On hover the words stay and the underline turns to the ink (was: a lighter accent for the words).

border-radius: var(--radius-control) (a pill); font-family: var(--font-body) at weight 600 in place of the heading face.

Primary is filled with the ink: background and border var(--color-accent), words var(--color-bg) (hover --color-neutral-200, pressed -300). Switched off, it is a flat grey pill, not a faded white one: background and border --color-neutral-800, words --color-neutral-600, opacity 1. A text field is a well: background: var(--color-bg) and a --color-neutral-600 edge (hover --color-neutral-400). Its caret and its focused edge keep var(--color-accent), which is the ink: a field in focus is framed in white (black in light), never in red.
The work-type badge is round: border-radius: var(--radius-chip); its letter is weight 700 (black on #ff0000 needs the heavier stroke).

The error notice gets its form once, as a shared class: the danger tint, the danger words, a bar of the danger colour down the left edge (box-shadow: inset var(--size-notice-bar) 0 0 var(--color-danger), so no size changes) and the word "Error" in front (::before, small capitals, weight 600). Nothing else in the app has a tinted box with a bar, and the accent is never red words, so an error cannot be taken for anything else.

FOR THE PM TO RULE. Direction D sets weight 600 on .btn, .dowToday and .errorNotice::before, and 700 on .glyph and .badge. Brief 103 moves weights into tokens and allows new --font-* names; the tile's rules allow no new --font-* name, so the tile holds the two numbers as literals. In the build they would be two tokens, for example --font-weight-strong: 600 and --font-weight-heavy: 700.

The rule that keeps five unrelated hues apart is replaced by the urgency-order rule (direction-d.json "typeScale"; check-tile.js checkUrgencyScale). One old assertion cannot hold: every pair dE at least 30. The chroma-spread assertion still passes by the numbers and no longer means anything. See the designer's report for the wording.
